theorem rhom_supported_quasiCoherent_pseudo_part
    (X : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ U : X.Opens, HasDerivedCategory.{w}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (K L : schemeDerivedCategory X)
    (hL : schemeDerivedQCohProperty X L)
    (hK : Scheme.IsPseudoCoherent X K) (hGE : ∃ a : ℤ, L.IsGE a) :
    schemeDerivedQCohProperty X
        ((derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toRingedSpace)
          X.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj (op K, L)) ∧
      ∀ x : X, ∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ ∃ a : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a →
        IsZero ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
            (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) n).obj
              ((derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toRingedSpace)
                X.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj (op K, L))))

title: Pseudo-coherent internal Hom quasi-coherence and local lower bounds
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and K,L objects of D(O_X) [def-pc-derived-category]. Assume L has quasi-coherent cohomology. If K is pseudo-coherent [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex] and there is an integer a such that H^n(L)=0 for all n<a, then RSheafHom(K,L) [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] has quasi-coherent cohomology and is locally bounded below: every point has an open neighbourhood on which all cohomology sheaves below some integer vanish.

proof.text: Choose a neighbourhood of each point on which K has a bounded-above finite-free representative, and shrink it to an affine open. The matrices of the differentials give a bounded-above finite-free module complex. Use the affine quasi-coherent derived equivalence to represent L there by a module complex. Exact restriction and exact, faithful tilde transfer the cohomological lower bound of L to that complex. The affine pseudo-coherent RHom calculation gives quasi-coherent cohomology and a lower bound for the internal Hom: if the source vanishes above b and the target below a, its Hom complex vanishes below a-b. The restriction isomorphism identifies this calculation with restriction of RHom(K,L). Quasi-coherence glues over the affine cover. The individual bounds give the claimed neighbourhood bound at each point; no finite cover or uniform global bound is required.
